sanskrit: śalyo 'pi rājan saṃkruddho nighnan somakapāṇḍavān punar eva śitair bāṇair yudhiṣṭhiram apīḍayat
english: Śalya too, O king, in fury slaying the Somakas and Pāṇḍavas, once more harried Yudhiṣṭhira with whetted arrows.

sanskrit: tasya bhīmo raṇe kruddhaḥ saṃdaṣṭadaśanacchadaḥ vināśāyābhisaṃdhāya gadām ādatta vīryavān
english: At this the valiant Bhīma, enraged in battle, biting his lip, resolved upon his destruction and took up his mace.

sanskrit: yamadaṇḍapratīkāśāṃ kālarātrim ivodyatām gajavājimanuṣyāṇāṃ prāṇāntakaraṇīm api
english: It was like the rod of Yama, raised aloft like the Night of Doom, the bringer of death to elephants, horses, and men.

sanskrit: hemapaṭṭaparikṣiptām ulkāṃ prajvalitām iva śaikyāṃ vyālīm ivātyugrāṃ vajrakalpām ayasmayīm
english: Wound about with bands of gold, like a blazing meteor, like a most fierce serpent slung in a cord, hard as the thunderbolt and wrought of iron.

sanskrit: candanāgurupaṅkāktāṃ pramadām īpsitām iva vasāmedosṛgādigdhāṃ jihvāṃ vaivasvatīm iva
english: Smeared with paste of sandal and aloe like a desired young woman, yet daubed with fat, marrow, and blood like the tongue of Yama, son of the Sun.

sanskrit: paṭughaṇṭāravaśatāṃ vāsavīm aśanīm iva nirmuktāśīviṣākārāṃ pṛktāṃ gajamadair api
english: Ringing with a hundred shrill bells like the thunderbolt of Vāsava, shaped like a venomous serpent freed from its skin, and slick with the ichor of elephants.

sanskrit: trāsanīṃ ripusainyānāṃ svasainyapariharṣiṇīm manuṣyaloke vikhyātāṃ giriśṛṅgavidāriṇīm
english: The terror of the enemy's hosts, the delight of his own troops, renowned in the world of men, the shatterer of mountain peaks.

sanskrit: yayā kailāsabhavane maheśvarasakhaṃ balī āhvayām āsa kaunteyaḥ saṃkruddham alakādhipam
english: With which the mighty son of Kuntī, in the dwelling on Kailāsa, had challenged in his wrath the lord of Alakā, the friend of Maheśvara.

sanskrit: yayā māyāvino dṛptān subahūn dhanadālaye jaghāna guhyakān kruddho mandārārthe mahābalaḥ nivāryamāṇo bahubhir draupadyāḥ priyam āsthitaḥ
english: With which the mighty one, enraged, slew in the abode of the Lord of Wealth many haughty Guhyakas skilled in illusion, for the sake of the mandāra blossoms, though warned off by many, intent upon Draupadī's pleasure.

sanskrit: tāṃ vajramaṇiratnaughām aṣṭāśriṃ vajragauravām samudyamya mahābāhuḥ śalyam abhyadravad raṇe
english: Raising that mace, set with masses of diamonds and gems, eight-sided and heavy as the thunderbolt, the mighty-armed one rushed upon Śalya in battle.

sanskrit: gadayā yuddhakuśalas tayā dāruṇanādayā pothayām āsa śalyasya caturo 'śvān mahājavān
english: Skilled in combat, with that mace of terrible roar he crushed the four swift-coursing horses of Śalya.

sanskrit: tataḥ śalyo raṇe kruddhaḥ pīne vakṣasi tomaram nicakhāna nadan vīro varma bhittvā ca so 'bhyagāt
english: Then Śalya, enraged in battle, with a roar drove a lance into Bhīma's broad chest, and the hero's weapon pierced through the armor and entered deep.

sanskrit: vṛkodaras tv asaṃbhrātas tam evoddhṛtya tomaram yantāraṃ madrarājasya nirbibheda tato hṛdi
english: But Vṛkodara, unshaken, plucked out that very lance and with it pierced the charioteer of the king of the Madras through the heart.

sanskrit: sa bhinnavarmā rudhiraṃ vaman vitrastamānasaḥ papātābhimukho dīno madrarājas tv apākramat
english: His armor cleft, vomiting blood, his spirit unnerved, the charioteer fell forward in his misery, and the king of the Madras drew back.

sanskrit: kṛtapratikṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā śalyo vismitamānasaḥ gadām āśritya dhīrātmā pratyamitram avaikṣata
english: Seeing the blow returned for blow, Śalya, his mind amazed, the steadfast one, leaning on his mace, looked upon his foe.

sanskrit: tataḥ sumanasaḥ pārthā bhīmasenam apūjayan tad dṛṣṭvā karma saṃgrāme ghoram akliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
english: Then the sons of Pṛthā, glad at heart, honored Bhīmasena, beholding that terrible deed in battle wrought by him whose works are tireless.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca patitaṃ prekṣya yantāraṃ śalyaḥ sarvāyasīṃ gadām ādāya tarasā rājaṃs tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing his charioteer fallen, Śalya, O king, swiftly took up his mace all of iron and stood firm as an unmoving mountain.

sanskrit: taṃ dīptam iva kālāgniṃ pāśahastam ivāntakam saśṛṅgam iva kailāsaṃ savajram iva vāsavam
english: Upon him, who was like the blazing fire of Doom, like Death with noose in hand, like Kailāsa with its peak, like Vāsava with his thunderbolt—

sanskrit: saśūlam iva haryakṣaṃ vane mattam iva dvipam javenābhyapatad bhīmaḥ pragṛhya mahatīṃ gadām
english: like the three-eyed Hari with his trident, like a rutting elephant in the forest—Bhīma rushed at speed, gripping his great mace.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhapraṇādaś ca tūryāṇāṃ ca sahasraśaḥ siṃhanādaś ca saṃjajñe śūrāṇāṃ harṣavardhanaḥ
english: Then arose the blare of conches and of trumpets in their thousands, and the lions' roar of the heroes, swelling their joy.

sanskrit: prekṣantaḥ sarvatas tau hi yodhā yodhamahādvipau tāvakāś ca pare caiva sādhu sādhv ity athābruvan
english: Watching from every side those two warriors, the great war-elephants among fighters, your men and the foe alike cried, 'Well done! Well done!'

sanskrit: na hi madrādhipād anyo rāmād vā yadunandanāt soḍhum utsahate vegaṃ bhīmasenasya saṃyuge
english: For none save the lord of the Madras, or Rāma the delight of the Yadus, could endure in combat the onset of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tathā madrādhipasyāpi gadāvegaṃ mahātmanaḥ soḍhum utsahate nānyo yodho yudhi vṛkodarāt
english: And likewise no other warrior in battle save Vṛkodara could endure the force of the great-souled lord of the Madras's mace.

sanskrit: tau vṛṣāv iva nardantau maṇḍalāni viceratuḥ āvalgitau gadāhastau madrarājavṛkodarau
english: Bellowing like two bulls, the king of the Madras and Vṛkodara, maces in hand, ranged in wheeling circles, leaping and bounding.

sanskrit: maṇḍalāvartamārgeṣu gadāviharaṇeṣu ca nirviśeṣam abhūd yuddhaṃ tayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ
english: In the wheeling, turning paths and in the flourishing of maces, the combat of those two lions among men was without distinction between them.

sanskrit: taptahemamayaiḥ śubhrair babhūva bhayavardhanī agnijvālair ivāviddhā paṭṭaiḥ śalyasya sā gadā
english: Wound about with bright bands of refined gold, that mace of Śalya grew terror-spreading, as though girt with tongues of fire.

sanskrit: tathaiva carato mārgān maṇḍaleṣu mahātmanaḥ vidyud abhrapratīkāśā bhīmasya śuśubhe gadā
english: And likewise, as the great-souled Bhīma ranged his paths in circles, his mace shone forth like lightning against a cloud.

sanskrit: tāḍitā madrarājena bhīmasya gadayā gadā dīpyamāneva vai rājan sasṛje pāvakārciṣaḥ
english: Struck by the king of the Madras, Bhīma's mace, as if ablaze, O king, gave off flashes of fire.

sanskrit: tathā bhīmena śalyasya tāḍitā gadayā gadā aṅgāravarṣaṃ mumuce tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And likewise Śalya's mace, struck by Bhīma's mace, scattered a rain of embers, and it seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: dantair iva mahānāgau śṛṅgair iva maharṣabhau tottrair iva tadānyonyaṃ gadāgrābhyāṃ nijaghnatuḥ
english: As two great elephants with their tusks, as two mighty bulls with their horns, as with goads, so then did they smite each other with the heads of their maces.

sanskrit: tau gadānihatair gātraiḥ kṣaṇena rudhirokṣitau prekṣaṇīyatarāv āstāṃ puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Their limbs battered by the maces and in a moment drenched with blood, the two grew yet fairer to behold, like two kiṃśuka trees in flower.

sanskrit: gadayā madrarājena savyadakṣiṇam āhataḥ bhīmaseno mahābāhur na cacālācalo yathā
english: Struck on left and right by the king of the Madras's mace, the mighty-armed Bhīmasena did not waver, like a mountain unmoved.

sanskrit: tathā bhīmagadāvegais tāḍyamāno muhur muhuḥ śalyo na vivyathe rājan dantinevāhato giriḥ
english: And likewise Śalya, battered again and again by the force of Bhīma's mace, did not flinch, O king, like a hill struck by a tusker.

sanskrit: śuśruve dikṣu sarvāsu tayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ gadānipātasaṃhrādo vajrayor iva nisvanaḥ
english: In all directions was heard the crash of the falling maces of those two lions among men, like the clap of two thunderbolts.

sanskrit: nivṛtya tu mahāvīryau samucchritagadāv ubhau punar antaramārgasthau maṇḍalāni viceratuḥ
english: Then those two of mighty valor, drawing back, both with maces uplifted, taking up positions on inner paths, ranged once more in wheeling circles.

sanskrit: athābhyetya padāny aṣṭau saṃnipāto 'bhavat tayoḥ udyamya lohadaṇḍābhyām atimānuṣakarmaṇoḥ
english: Then, advancing eight paces, those two of superhuman deeds came together in collision, raising their iron clubs.

sanskrit: prārthayānau tadānyo 'nyaṃ maṇḍalāni viceratuḥ kriyāviśeṣaṃ kṛtinau darśayām āsatus tadā
english: Each seeking the other's life, they ranged in circles, and those two adepts then displayed their special skill.

sanskrit: athodyamya gade ghore saśṛṅgāv iva parvatau tāv ājaghnatur anyonyaṃ yathā bhūmicale 'calau
english: Then, raising their terrible maces, like two mountains with their peaks, they smote each other as two hills in an earthquake.

sanskrit: tau parasparavegāc ca gadābhyāṃ ca bhṛśāhatau yugapat petatur vīrāv ubhāv indradhvajāv iva
english: By each other's force and grievously struck by the maces, both heroes fell together at once, like two banners of Indra.

sanskrit: ubhayoḥ senayor vīrās tadā hāhākṛto 'bhavan bhṛśaṃ marmaṇy abhihatāv ubhāv āstāṃ suvihvalau
english: The heroes of both armies then raised a cry of dismay; both, struck hard in their vitals, lay sorely stricken.

sanskrit: tataḥ sagadam āropya madrāṇām ṛṣabhaṃ rathe apovāha kṛpaḥ śalyaṃ tūrṇam āyodhanād api
english: Then Kṛpa, lifting onto his chariot, mace and all, that bull of the Madras, swiftly bore Śalya away from the battle.

sanskrit: kṣībavad vihvalatvāt tu nimeṣāt punar utthitaḥ bhīmaseno gadāpāṇiḥ samāhvayata madrapam
english: But, swaying as if drunk in his daze, Bhīmasena rose again in a twinkling and, mace in hand, summoned the lord of the Madras.

sanskrit: tatas tu tāvakāḥ śūrā nānāśastrasamāyutāḥ nānāvāditraśabdena pāṇḍusenām ayodhayan
english: Then your heroes, furnished with weapons of every kind, with the din of many instruments did battle against the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: bhujāv ucchritya śastraṃ ca śabdena mahatā tataḥ abhyadravan mahārāja duryodhanapurogamāḥ
english: Raising their arms and weapons, with a mighty shout, O great king, they charged, with Duryodhana at their head.

sanskrit: tad anīkam abhiprekṣya tatas te pāṇḍunandanāḥ prayayuḥ siṃhanādena duryodhanavadhepsayā
english: Beholding that host, the sons of Pāṇḍu then advanced with a lion's roar, eager to slay Duryodhana.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ tūrṇaṃ putras te bharatarṣabha prāsena cekitānaṃ vai vivyādha hṛdaye bhṛśam
english: As they rushed swiftly on, your son, O bull of the Bhāratas, with a barbed dart pierced Cekitāna sorely in the heart.

sanskrit: sa papāta rathopasthe tava putreṇa tāḍitaḥ rudhiraughapariklinnaḥ praviśya vipulaṃ tamaḥ
english: Struck by your son, he fell upon the floor of his chariot, drenched in a flood of blood, sinking into deep darkness.

sanskrit: cekitānaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ prasaktam abhyavarṣanta śaravarṣāṇi bhāgaśaḥ
english: Seeing Cekitāna slain, the great car-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas poured down, each in his quarter, unbroken showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tāvakānām anīkeṣu pāṇḍavā jitakāśinaḥ vyacaranta mahārāja prekṣaṇīyāḥ samantataḥ
english: Amid the ranks of your men the Pāṇḍavas, flushed with victory, ranged about, O great king, a sight to behold on every side.

sanskrit: kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca saubalaś ca mahābalaḥ ayodhayan dharmarājaṃ madrarājapuraskṛtāḥ
english: Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarman, and the mighty son of Subala did battle against the King of Righteousness, with the king of the Madras at their fore.

sanskrit: bhāradvājasya hantāraṃ bhūrivīryaparākramam duryodhano mahārāja dhṛṣṭadyumnam ayodhayat
english: Duryodhana, O great king, did battle against Dhṛṣṭadyumna, slayer of the son of Bharadvāja, a man of abounding valor and prowess.

sanskrit: trisāhasrā rathā rājaṃs tava putreṇa coditāḥ ayodhayanta vijayaṃ droṇaputrapuraskṛtāḥ
english: Three thousand chariots, O king, urged on by your son and led by Droṇa's son, did battle against the Conqueror.

sanskrit: vijaye dhṛtasaṃkalpāḥ samabhityaktajīvitāḥ prāviśaṃs tāvakā rājan haṃsā iva mahat saraḥ
english: Fixed in their resolve for victory, having wholly cast away their lives, your men plunged in, O king, like swans into a great lake.

sanskrit: tato yuddham abhūd ghoraṃ parasparavadhaiṣiṇām anyonyavadhasaṃyuktam anyonyaprītivardhanam
english: Then there was a terrible battle between those who craved each other's death, a slaughter of one another that yet swelled their mutual delight.

sanskrit: tasmin pravṛtte saṃgrāme rājan vīravarakṣaye anileneritaṃ ghoram uttasthau pārthivaṃ rajaḥ
english: When that battle was joined, O king, that destroyer of the best of heroes, a terrible dust of the earth, stirred by the wind, arose.

sanskrit: śravaṇān nāmadheyānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca kīrtanāt parasparaṃ vijānīmo ye cāyudhyann abhītavat
english: By the hearing of their names and by the proclaiming of the Pāṇḍavas' names we knew one another, and those who fought on without fear.

sanskrit: tad rajaḥ puruṣavyāghra śoṇitena praśāmitam diśaś ca vimalā jajñus tasmin rajasi śāmite
english: That dust, O tiger among men, was laid by blood, and when the dust was stilled the quarters of the sky grew clear.

sanskrit: tathā pravṛtte saṃgrāme ghorarūpe bhayānake tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca nāsīt kaś cit parāṅmukhaḥ
english: As that battle raged on, of terrible form and dreadful, among your men and the foe there was not one who turned his back.

sanskrit: brahmalokaparā bhūtvā prārthayanto jayaṃ yudhi suyuddhena parākrāntā narāḥ svargam abhīpsavaḥ
english: Setting Brahmā's world above all, seeking victory in battle, men strove valiantly by fair fighting, longing for heaven.

sanskrit: bhartṛpiṇḍavimokṣārthaṃ bhartṛkāryaviniścitāḥ svargasaṃsaktamanaso yodhā yuyudhire tadā
english: To discharge the debt of their lord's bread, resolved upon their lord's cause, their minds fixed on heaven, the warriors fought on then.

sanskrit: nānārūpāṇi śastrāṇi visṛjanto mahārathāḥ anyonyam abhigarjantaḥ praharantaḥ parasparam
english: Loosing weapons of many forms, the great car-warriors roared at one another and struck each other.

sanskrit: hata vidhyata gṛhṇīta praharadhvaṃ nikṛntata iti sma vācaḥ śrūyante tava teṣāṃ ca vai bale
english: 'Strike! Pierce! Seize! Smite! Cut him down!'—such cries were heard in your host and in theirs.

sanskrit: tataḥ śalyo mahārāja dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram vivyādha niśitair bāṇair hantukāmo mahāratham
english: Then Śalya, O great king, longing to slay him, pierced the King of Righteousness Yudhiṣṭhira, that great car-warrior, with whetted arrows.

sanskrit: tasya pārtho mahārāja nārācān vai caturdaśa marmāṇy uddiśya marmajño nicakhāna hasann iva
english: At him the son of Pṛthā, O great king, knowing the vital points, drove fourteen iron shafts, aiming at those points, as if with a smile.

sanskrit: taṃ vārya pāṇḍavaṃ bāṇair hantukāmo mahāyaśāḥ vivyādha samare kruddho bahubhiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: Checking the Pāṇḍava with arrows and longing to slay him, the man of great renown, enraged, pierced him in battle with many heron-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: atha bhūyo mahārāja śareṇa nataparvaṇā yudhiṣṭhiraṃ samājaghne sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: Then again, O great king, with a smooth-jointed arrow he struck Yudhiṣṭhira hard, before the eyes of all the host.

sanskrit: dharmarājo 'pi saṃkruddho madrarājaṃ mahāyaśāḥ vivyādha niśitair bāṇaiḥ kaṅkabarhiṇavājitaiḥ
english: The King of Righteousness too, of great renown, in fury pierced the king of the Madras with whetted arrows fledged with heron and peacock feathers.

sanskrit: candrasenaṃ ca saptatyā sūtaṃ ca navabhiḥ śaraiḥ drumasenaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā nijaghāna mahārathaḥ
english: That great car-warrior struck down Candrasena with seventy arrows, the charioteer with nine, and Drumasena with sixty-four.

sanskrit: cakrarakṣe hate śalyaḥ pāṇḍavena mahātmanā nijaghāna tato rājaṃś cedīn vai pañcaviṃśatim
english: His wheel-guards slain by the great-souled Pāṇḍava, Śalya then, O king, struck down five-and-twenty of the Cedis.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ pañcaviṃśatyā bhīmasenaṃ ca pañcabhiḥ mādrīputrau śatenājau vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: He pierced Sātyaki with five-and-twenty, Bhīmasena with five, and the two sons of Mādrī in battle with a hundred whetted arrows.

sanskrit: evaṃ vicaratas tasya saṃgrāme rājasattama saṃpreṣayac chitān pārthaḥ śarān āśīviṣopamān
english: As he ranged thus in the battle, O best of kings, the son of Pṛthā sent forth whetted arrows like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: dhvajāgraṃ cāsya samare kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ pramukhe vartamānasya bhallenāpaharad rathāt
english: And the son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira, with a broad-headed shaft struck the crest of his banner from his chariot as he stood at the forefront of battle.

sanskrit: pāṇḍuputreṇa vai tasya ketuṃ chinnaṃ mahātmanā nipatantam apaśyāma giriśṛṅgam ivāhatam
english: We saw his standard, cut down by the great-souled son of Pāṇḍu, falling like a mountain peak struck asunder.

sanskrit: dhvajaṃ nipatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavaṃ ca vyavasthitam saṃkruddho madrarājo 'bhūc charavarṣaṃ mumoca ha
english: Seeing his banner fallen and the Pāṇḍava holding firm, the king of the Madras grew enraged and loosed a rain of arrows.

sanskrit: śalyaḥ sāyakavarṣeṇa parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān abhyavarṣad ameyātmā kṣatriyaṃ kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ
english: Śalya, that bull among Kṣatriyas of measureless soul, rained down with a shower of arrows upon that Kṣatriya, as the rain-cloud pours its showers.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ bhīmasenaṃ ca mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau ekaikaṃ pañcabhir viddhvā yudhiṣṭhiram apīḍayat
english: Piercing Sātyaki, Bhīmasena, and the two sons of Mādrī, the Pāṇḍavas, each with five arrows, he harried Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tato bāṇamayaṃ jālaṃ vitataṃ pāṇḍavorasi apaśyāma mahārāja meghajālam ivodgatam
english: Then we saw a net of arrows spread over the breast of the Pāṇḍava, O great king, like a mass of clouds risen up.

sanskrit: tasya śalyo raṇe kruddho bāṇaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ diśaḥ pracchādayām āsa pradiśaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Śalya, that great car-warrior, enraged in battle, with his smooth-jointed arrows covered over the quarters and the intermediate quarters of the sky.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā bāṇajālena pīḍitaḥ babhūva hṛtavikrānto jambho vṛtrahaṇā yathā
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, oppressed by the net of arrows, was robbed of his valor, as Jambha was by the slayer of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca pīḍite dharmarāje tu madrarājena māriṣa sātyakir bhīmasenaś ca mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau parivārya rathaiḥ śalyaṃ pīḍayām āsur āhave
english: Saṃjaya said: When the King of Righteousness was hard-pressed by the king of the Madras, O honored one, Sātyaki and Bhīmasena and the two sons of Mādrī, the Pāṇḍavas, surrounded Śalya with their chariots and beset him in the battle.
